items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: he called me up in latrine, and he said, “Danny, a levy’s come down from Washington and you’re being transferred someplace in the Orient. We don’t know where yet, but we’re going to call Sergeant Shipp,” who had already been transferred over there

ctx.x: I showed you how I got in and all this and that. So now we’re over on Staten Island with the New York Army Band and a levy comes down from Washington. Man, I was the drummer with the stage band. And everybody figured well D’Imperio’s never going to get transferred out of here because there’s nobody to replace him. And our First Sergeant’s name was Joe College, or Howard Joe College, we called him J.C. And he said these — J.C.’s man they’re just not going to be able to take him away, you know. Well the Army…

band was Carter Jefferson, the tenor player who was with Woody Shaw for years, with the Jazz Messengers, you know, later on. But he didn’t know anything about — he had been with Little Richard and Jackie Wilson, bands like that. He was a black saxophone player from Washington. And I brought a bunch of tapes of Charlie Parker and this and that, which then I bought an Ampex reel to reel and we used to just sit and listen to that stuff and that’s sort of the way he developed into a fine jazz player. He’s since gone…
